newsitem.title: UK: Allied plays down Teachers sales decline.
newsitem.headline: Allied plays down Teachers sales decline.

text.p: Allied Domecq Plc on Wednesday played down reports that its Teachers whisky brand had suffered a sharp fall in sales and said the decline reflected its decision to cut out low-margin business.

A spokesman for Allied, who asked not to be named, told Reuters that the decline in Teachers sales was due to a company policy to build global premium brands and that the profitability of the brand had improved.
"If you dig a bit deeper than the volume figures you find that the performance in value terms is quite impressive," the spokesman said.

He said advertising spending on Teachers had doubled in the past year, "and the result is that despite the volume loss and increased investment the value of the brand has shown a significant improvement."
He also pointed out that Teachers sales in the UK were only one percent of the company's global spirits sales.

Earlier Allied shares dipped in a rising market as analysts at SocGen repeated a "reduce" rating on the stock, following data quoted by Highland Distilleries Plc showing falling Teachers sales in the second half of last year.
The figures, from research group Stats MR, showed Teachers sales down 28.6 percent in supermarkets and other retailers and by 14 percent in the licensed trade.
Yet the Allied spokesman said the company was happy with the brand's performance. "Acutally it is a very strong story," he said. "It is a position we are very happy with."
Allied shares were down 2p at 442 by 1145 GMT in modest volume of 766,908 shares.
